candidates.source_body_excerpt: The kick pitch is located by The Burnside Centre in Middleton. Residents in Middleton are campaigning for a replacement football pitch after plans were announced to turn the existing site into a car park. Campaigners say the pitch in Burnside Crescent on the Langley Estate is a community hub as well as somewhere people can play football and other sports. The pitch, which is next to the Burnside Centre, is one of three on the estate, and the car park will be for the centre. Families say they have been told replacement facilities will be provided at Rochdale AFC and Rochdale Council's planned Football and Community Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee Playing Fields. But they are campaigning for the new pitch to be created on land next to the original. The Burnside Centre said it understands why people are disappointed to see the pitch decommissioned, but said one of the reasons the decision was made related to concerns about antisocial behaviour. It added: "The pitch, which dates back to the late 1990s, had reached the end of its expected lifespan and required significant investment to remain operational." Resident Kelly Burton has four children, three of whom use the football pitch regularly.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A councillor has been praised for his response after dating app images and details of him were shared on social media with calls for him to quit. Images of North Heywood Cllr Paul O’Neill’s Grindr profile were shared yesterday with posts saying a “public figure should be more discreate with his personal life” while a second said “another Labour councillor soon to be out”. But in a move that has received plenty of support, Cllr O’Neill responded on Facebook last night, including an image of himself enjoying a pint of Murphy’s, whose memorable slogan was “like the Murphy’s, I’m not bitter”. Cllr O’Neill added: “It’s been brought to my attention that two people have decided to visit a gay men’s dating app I’m a member of, create an account for themselves, and then find my profile, screen shot it, and share it on social media, complete with some rather unpleasant comments. “The reasons why those people decided to create gay dating accounts for themselves were ‘curiosity’ and ‘verifying’ that I had a profile, apparently. “I’m glad that my photos were recent, as I’ve lost three stone since February. I’m only sorry these two characters couldn’t wait a few more weeks before invading my privacy, as I’ve just started going back to the gym, and I might have looked even more fabulous than I already did at the Manchester Pride 2026 event most of the photos are from. “Joking aside, there are more revealing photos of many straight men and women at the beach or at the gym all over social media, I am not remotely ashamed to have a social and dating life, and it obviously affects not a jot my work as a proud ward councillor for the brilliant people of North Heywood. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Jamie Dale said rehabilitated ex-offenders need to be part of the support process for prison leavers A former prisoner who runs a support network for ex-offenders said government plans to release inmates early would fail to ease prison overcrowding without support from people who had experienced the system themselves. Jamie Dale, 47, from Rochdale, in Greater Manchester, spent more than 11 years in prison for his involvement in organised crime. He now runs the Old Lags Network, which aims to cut reoffending and bridge the gap between prison and the community. He said many prisoners "fall through the cracks" after release. "Most of the people who return quite quickly have not got great family networks," he said. Dale set up the Old Lags Network in September 2025 to provide support to prison leavers Dale said involving ex-offenders in developing solutions would "drastically reduce the amount of people being recalled to prison". "A lot of them can just end up sleeping on the streets," he said.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Liverpool U21s head coach Rob Page lauded the character of his side after producing a remarkable comeback to draw 3-3 at Rochdale in the Jersey Mike's Trophy. Despite playing 70 minutes with 10 men and trailing 3-1 entering second-half stoppage time, the young Reds avoided defeat in their northern Group H opener on Tuesday night. Substitutes Ben Trueman and Josh Sonni-Lambie netted in minutes 94 and 96 respectively to level the affair and take it to a penalty shootout, which Page's side won 7-6 to claim a bonus point. Speaking to reporters afterwards, Page said: "I mean, what character and resilience the boys showed to come back not only from the sending-off early on in the game, but to show character to see the game through. "I thought the substitutes came on and made a difference, gave us the fresh legs in the middle of the park that we needed. So, nothing but praise for that." He added: "We talk about being proud to wear the jersey. And when you wear the badge, there comes a level of expectation when you go out and play for Liverpool. "So, they know that myself and Jay [Spearing], who's played for the club, won't accept anything less than 100 per cent. So, they've got that built-in resilience. It's the character that we want in the team. "We've tried to change the mentality certainly in the 12 months that I've been here and I'm seeing it every day in training. The intensity of training has increased and they've got that winning mentality.

This October, Rochdale residents have a rewarding new reason to lace up their walking boots and step outdoors. The charity Hearing Dogs for Deaf People is inviting the local community to explore the town’s scenic trails, historic landmarks, and hidden gems on foot- all while raising vital funds to transform the lives of deaf people across the region. The autumn initiative, known as the Great British Dog Walk, challenges participants to clock up a total of 70 miles throughout the month. Supported by the charity’s active puppy training hub based right in Rochdale, the campaign encourages walkers of all ages and abilities to discover new corner-of-the-map adventures or simply add extra distance to their favourite everyday routes. Every step taken carries a powerful meaning behind the mileage. The 70-mile target symbolises the average £70,000 lifetime cost to train and support a single, life-changing hearing dog. By turning routine strolls into sponsored miles, local participants will directly help fund the careful breeding, puppy socialisation, and specialised training required to match these remarkable dogs with those who need them most.

Photographers and writers have made a mythology around the band due to exposure in the music press. Girl B was allegedly exploited in the mid 2000s. Girl A was said to have been abused in the same period. While the alleged abuse of another, Girl C, allegedly began in the late 1980s. The trio were ‘groomed', 'manipulated' and became 'sex slaves', often being forced to have sex ‘with multiple men on the same day, in filthy flats and houses’, prosecutors allege. Click here to hear the latest from Manchester's courts in our newsletter Tahir Rashid, 55; Mohammed Saleem, 47; Sucklane Shah, 47; Amjad Mahmood, 54; Iftaq Hussain, 46; and Arshad Mohammed, 56, deny all the charges they face. As the trial at Minshull Street Crown Court continued, Girl B was cross-examined in court by Mr Rashid’s barrister, Ayaz Qazi KC. Mr Qazi claimed that Girl B had given ‘limited details’ about Mr Rashid. He put it to her: “I’m going to suggest that the reason you are able to give very limited details about [Mr Rashid] is because they are details you have picked up from [Girl A].” Girl B replied: “No, because if she remembered more she would have told me more, if I was making it up I could have said more. I’m only saying what I remember.” Jurors heard that Girl A and Girl B lost touch but began messaging each other again as adults. Mr Qazi referenced messages from Girl A which mentioned compensation. Asked whether she had received compensation, Girl B said: “I got £20,000 which was from social services, and then I got £69,000 from the CICA [Criminal Injuries Compensation Authority].” Asked for the total figure she received, Girl B said: “It would have been £89.000.” Girl B claims she was raped by Mr Rashid at his home in Rochdale. Girl B said she had exchanged messages with Girl A, but that this was not just about ‘this case and this operation’, and that ‘there was other things we spoke about’. Mr Rashid, of Hudsons Walk, Rochdale, denies 12 counts of rape; three counts of indecent assault; and one count of assault by penetration. Mr Mohammed, of Merefield Street, Rochdale, denies four counts of rape; and one count of assault by penetration. The charges include allegations against Girl A and Girl B. Mr Hussain, of Hey Street, Rochdale, denies three counts of rape allegedly committed against Girl A. Mr Mahmood, of Channing Street, Rochdale, denies 11 counts of rape, two counts of indecency with a child, two counts of assault by penetration and one count of indecent assault. The charges include allegations against Girl A and Girl B. Proceeding .

candidates.source_body_excerpt: WHEN the Rochdale women’s team takes to the field for its Northern League 1 fixtures at the Hive, there is an international flavour to the line-up courtesy of an initiative put in place by Hornets General Manager Matt Rigby. Having spent ten years helping develop rugby league in the Netherlands across various roles, including coaching the first national women’s team, Rigby was keen to find a way of benefiting his past and present organisations. “My connection with rugby league in the Netherlands goes back around 10 years, so it is a country and a programme that I have a real personal connection with,” Rigby told Rugby League World. “I spent the last two years involved with the Netherlands Women’s National Team, so I have seen first-hand the potential that exists there. “When you don’t have a domestic competition, it is incredibly difficult for players to develop consistently. For me, bringing players into Rochdale is about giving them an environment where they can play at a good level and experience what it is like to be part of a functioning club programme. For the players, being able to play alongside our women’s team gives them far more exposure to the game than they would otherwise have access to at home. “At the same time, it benefits Rochdale. We get players who are hungry to learn, experience different coaching and bring a different perspective into the group. It is very much a two-way relationship.” Speaking to the Netherlands players, who pay for their own flights to the United Kingdom while Rigby stumps up for their accommodation, the Rochdale experience is as much about a social and cultural exchange as it is about developing their games. “In the Netherlands, we don’t have a rugby league culture, so playing for Rochdale has given me the opportunity to fully experience it,” Vera Van Der Zwan, a physical education teacher from Zwolle and the first Netherlands women’s team captain, explained.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans to turn delipidated former storage units into flats have been thrown out over issues with bin collections. Ghulam Hadhar applied to Rochdale Council for permission to create seven self-contained apartments at 24a Baron Street, on the edge of Rochdale town centre. Planning documents describe the U-shaped building overlooking a courtyard as being is in a state of disrepair. They add: “The proposed development will bring a mostly disused existing building and wider site into a suitable and sustainable use which is currently open to crime, dumping and anti-social behaviour, and could become an eyesore over time. “It is positioned in a prominent location in the town centre, and an opportunity has arisen where investment can be made to bring the building to a suitable functional use and where it would not have a negative impact on the surrounding area. “Minimal changes are made externally to the building. The proposal involves the removal of existing roller shutters to doors and windows and the insertion of new windows and doors at ground and first-floor level which would include sandstone head and cills to match the existing. “The courtyard area would provide good-sized outdoor amenity space retained to the rear of the site for future residents.” The plans include creating a bin storage area with the bins to be collected from Oldham Road, but issues have been raised over rights of way.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Fireworks will return to the region’s biggest park as the borough gets ready for Bonfire Night. As well as fireworks in Rochdale, Heywood and Middleton, celebrations will return to Heaton Park for the first time in seven years. Manchester City Council last held firework celebrations in its parks in 2019 but they will return this year on Saturday, November 7. The council has decided not to include bonfires, with the entertainment focusing instead on free family-friendly fireworks to “bring communities together”. Another change will see two different displays at the parks, with a reduced-noise display held at 5pm for families and SEND audiences, followed at 8pm with the main fireworks displays. Cllr Garry Bridges, Leader of Manchester City Council said: “Residents tell us how important it is to create opportunities for our communities to come together and celebrate. “Our fireworks display is exactly one of those events that bridge culture and background – and so it’s fantastic to bring back these free community displays that give families, friends and neighbours a shared experience.” Earlier in the week, on Monday, November 2, Rochdale Council will be holding the first of its three Bonfire Night events, with a firework display and family funfair at at Bowlee Community Park in Middleton.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Planners have given their blessing for the site of a former church to become homes. Zest Eco applied to Rochdale Council to build seven new houses on land at Egerton Street — the former New Jerusalem Church — in Middleton, which was founded before 1886 and was demolished by 2012. In planning documents, Zest said: “The proposal delivers seven three-bedroom family dwellings, each with private gardens and dedicated parking. “This form of development responds directly to the identified need for family housing rather than higher-density flat accommodation. “Full planning permission is sought for the erection of seven 2.5-storey three-bedroom townhouses with rear dormers, solar panels, associated parking, private gardens, landscaping and vehicular access via a new dropped kerb from Egerton Street. “The proposal regenerates a vacant brownfield site to deliver family housing within an established residential neighbourhood, respecting local character, safeguarding neighbouring amenity and providing safe and efficient access arrangements.” There were five objections to the plans, including a loss of on-street parking for existing residents, overdevelopment of the site and the loss of green space. candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Rochdale lifted themselves off the foot of the League Two table with a 2-0 win against Oldham in their Greater Manchester derby.

The home side took the lead just seven minutes in. Charlie Tasker and Jonny Smith combined down the right, and Tasker's low delivery in behind the retreating Oldham defence was swept into the roof of the net by Dan Moss.

Oldham frontman Mike Fondop missed a gilt-edged chance on 25 minutes, sliding the ball wide of the post with an open goal at his mercy after a mistake from Dale stopper Nils Ramming, who had his pocket picked by Keenan Appiah-Forson.

The visitors continued to press forward after the interval, Kane Drummond's delivery across the face of goal eluding Fondop and substitute Calum Kavanagh.

Dale delivered a sucker punch when they doubled the lead on 62 minutes. Latics keeper Matt Hudson's kick towards the halfway line was met by Baba Adeeko, who headed the ball forward for Dajaune Brown to advance into the penalty area, side-step Donervon Daniels and slam a firm drive into the bottom corner.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale boss Ian Watson praised his players for adapting to the demands of the Greater Manchester derby clash against Oldham following their 2-0 win at the Crown Oil Arena. Dan Moss’ seventh-minute opener eased the tension around the stadium, fans having called for Watson’s head in the previous home fixture, a 4-1 loss against Gillingham. Oldham spurned several chances before Dajaune Brown doubled the lead for Dale in the 62nd minute. The win lifted Watson’s men off the foot of the League Two table and secured bragging rights over their near neighbours. “Derby days bring a lot of tension and nerves and probably suit a different style than the one we like to play, these games are full of chaos,” said Watson. “But I thought we adapted and found a way to win the game incredibly well. Today was just about getting a result for the fans and for the club. The scoreboard was all that mattered. “The performance wasn’t where we want it to be, but derby days are almost an isolated case where you just need the scoreboard right and to get a good feeling around the club. “I’m incredibly proud of the boys. We’d spoken all week about what this game means to the fans and how much we wanted to run and duel with the opposition to show how much it means to us, and I thought the players did that.” In between Dale’s goals, Oldham had created several openings. Mike Fondop headed a good chance over and then fired wide with an open goal at his mercy after a mistake from Dale goalkeeper Nils Ramming. Oldham manager Micky Mellon was bitterly disappointed his side were unable to reward the travelling supporters and accepted responsibility for the result would fall on his shoulders.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Oldham Athletic suffered derby day defeat for the first time in a decade in the league. Latics looked comfortable in possession in the opening exchanges, albeit without doing anything to hurt Rochdale. But they were stung in the eighth minute when a cross from the right was flicked on in the box and Oldham looked to make amends from that early defensive lapse and carved out a number of openings. But they failed to capitalise on any of them. Just five minutes after falling behind Kane Drummond whipped a good ball into the box, Mike Fondop climbed to meet it but could not keep his free header down. Rochdale then struggled to deal with an Ollie Norburn corner that he sent to the far post, the ball was only half cleared but Gus Scott-Morriss' header was too tame to trouble goalkeeper Nils Ramming. But the worst of the misses came just before the half-hour. Keenan Appiah-Forson did well to put Ramming under pressure and force the keeper to lose control of the ball, it rolled for Fondop, but the striker put his low shot narrowly wide with an open goal at his mercy.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale lifted themselves off the foot of the League Two table with a 2-0 win against Oldham in their Greater Manchester derby. The home side took the lead just seven minutes in. Charlie Tasker and Jonny Smith combined down the right, and Tasker’s low delivery in behind the retreating Oldham defence was swept into the roof of the net by Dan Moss. Oldham frontman Mike Fondop missed a gilt-edged chance on 25 minutes, sliding the ball wide of the post with an open goal at his mercy after a mistake from Dale stopper Nils Ramming, who had his pocket picked by Keenan Appiah-Forson. The visitors continued to press forward after the interval, Kane Drummond’s delivery across the face of goal eluding Fondop and substitute Calum Kavanagh. Dale delivered a sucker punch when they doubled the lead on 62 minutes. Latics keeper Matt Hudson’s kick towards the halfway line was met by Baba Adeeko, who headed the ball forward for Dajaune Brown to advance into the penalty area, side-step Donervon Daniels and slam a firm drive into the bottom corner.

The Heywood Community Gala advert depicted large fairground rides and promised a family funfair, live music and DJs, street food and children's entertainment.

The event was advertised as running from Friday 18 September until Sunday 20 September at The Pig and Whistle in Heywood.

Its promotional image generated by AI depicts large fairground rides, performers, balloons and crowds alongside a list of attractions including licensed bars, face painting, children's characters and games and information stalls.

Photos supplied from the venue on Saturday morning show around eight gazebos outside. The large fairground rides depicted in the promotional artwork are not visible in the photographs.

The difference has prompted comparisons on Facebook with the Willy Wonka-themed experience in Glasgow which attracted widespread attention in 2024 after visitors complained that the reality did not match its elaborate promotional imagery.

A Facebook page called Cameron Boland - Scam Event Watch & Awareness has been criticising the Heywood event and previously alleged it was a scam. The page can be found here; https://www.facebook.com/profile.php?id=100095319109710

In its latest post, the page claimed Cameron Boland had said some of the biggest costs involved in the gala were security, staging and infrastructure, and production and entertainment.

The page alleged there was no stage and claimed performers were appearing on a rug between tables. It also questioned the security arrangements.

Those claims have not been independently verified; however, there have been multiple events captured by this page.

The same page published a warning on 9 September telling traders not to pay money upfront for stalls and made further allegations concerning previous events linked to Mr Boland.

A very similar event by the same organiser was forced to be cancelled by Salford City Council and GMP, the same 3-day event on 18, 19 and 20 August.

Those allegations have not been established as fact.

The photographs show activity taking place at The Pig and Whistle on Saturday but cannot establish everything available at the venue during the three-day event.

The tenant and operator of The Pig & Whistle, Kelly, defended the decision

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Members, volunteers, partners, staff and community supporters celebrated a year of significant achievements and the difference Kashmir Youth Project continues to make across Rochdale. KYP’s annual general and public meetings provided an opportunity to share its progress throughout 2025/26, celebrate the contribution of its staff and volunteers, and engage with members, partners and the wider community about the organisation’s work and priorities for the year ahead. Across advice and welfare, learning and skills, adult day care and community food pantry, KYP recorded 11,259 engagements and visits across its services during the year. The group also worked with more than 80 organisations and agencies, delivering more than 200 community events and activities, helping to strengthen partnerships and create opportunities for people across Rochdale. KYP’s work has generated significant financial and social value for local residents, securing £2 million in financial gains for people across the borough. This impact was delivered through 3,526 client interventions, providing vital advice, guidance and support to those who needed it most. Its Advice and Welfare Outreach locations have also continued to grow, expanding its reach into Heywood and Middleton and increasing from five outreach centres to 11 across the borough. This expansion has enabled KYP to support more residents in accessing the advice, services and opportunities they need to improve their lives. Learning and skills remained a key area of activity, with 8,460 learning hours delivered and 164 people supported into further training and employment.
